items.summary: Watch out for unexpected recovery emails and invitations.

1Password confirms hackers stole customer data, but not their passwords

Watch out for unexpected recovery emails and invitations.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 12:05 AM ET

•

•

1Password

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• 1Password has confirmed a security breach that exposed some customers’ personal information, including names and email addresses.

• The company says no customer passwords were exposed and that users don’t need to change their account or saved passwords.

• 1Password recommends watching out for unexpected account recovery emails and invitations following the breach.

Trust is everything when you’re in the business of keeping people’s passwords safe. It’s a responsibility that has only grown for 1Password in recent months, with the company enabling Claude and, more recently, other AI agents to sign into websites without exposing users’ credentials. That trust is now being put to the test after 1Password confirmed a security breach that exposed some customer information, although it maintains that users’ passwords are safe.

In a blog post published on November 25, 1Password revealed that it began investigating the breach on November 19 after detecting suspicious activity involving an employee’s corporate GitHub account. The attacker gained access to the company’s source code and compromised backend services, obtaining customer names, email addresses, account identifiers, and other account information.

However, 1Password maintains that neither customer vaults nor the encryption keys protecting them were compromised. The company doesn’t store your account password or Secret Key, so you don’t need to change your 1Password password or any passwords saved in your vault. The company says it has secured the affected systems, changed potentially exposed internal credentials, and strengthened its account recovery and invitation verification process. It hasn’t disclosed how many customers were affected.

This isn’t 1Password’s first security scare. In October 2023, the company disclosed an incident linked to a breach at Okta, although no customer data was accessed at the time. Rival LastPass suffered a more serious breach in 2022, with hackers eventually obtaining copies of customer password vaults. As recently as June 2026, LastPass suffered another data breach that exposed customers’ personal information but left their saved passwords untouched.

For now, 1Password users should be particularly wary of unexpected account recovery emails and invitations. Hackers could use the stolen information to make phishing attempts more convincing. So if the incident makes you uncomfortable sticking with 1Password, Android has a safer way to move passwords and passkeys between password managers without exporting your entire vault in plain text.

items.body: A MacBook Air with a new look could launch in late 2027 or 2028, Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman said in the latest episode of his Power On podcast. Apple plans to refresh the ‌MacBook Air‌ with M6 chips in early 2027 alongside the MacBook Neo 2, but that update won't include a new design. A more extensive overhaul could follow later in 2027 or in 2028, and the ‌MacBook Air‌ could get an OLED display at that time. MacBook Air is Apple's most popular computer, and they need to keep it very fresh. And so my anticipation is 2027, 2028 is when we're going to get the big MacBook Air overhaul. And I think OLED will be part of that conversation. Apple last overhauled the ‌MacBook Air‌'s design in 2022, eliminating the prior wedge shape for a more uniform MacBook Pro-style chassis. The machine adopted a brighter Liquid Retina display with a notch for the camera, and a MagSafe charging port. In 2023, Apple added a 15-inch model, but since then, we've only gotten minor updates. Apple just added ‌OLED‌ to the MacBook Pro with the launch of the 2026 PROLED models, so it's not clear whether the high-end display will trickle down to the ‌MacBook Air‌ that quickly. In prior reports , Gurman has leaned more toward the 2028 timeline than late 2027. Pricing on the PROLED ‌MacBook Pro‌ starts at $2,899, while the ‌MacBook Air‌ is one of Apple's more affordable notebooks and starts at $1,299. Apple would likely need to offer a high-end ‌OLED‌ ‌MacBook Air‌ alongside ‌MacBook Air‌ models with an LCD display to keep the price gap intact. Google Home is sorting out issues with speakers, cameras, lights, and more

Your smart home sounds like it's about to get a little bit smarter.

•

TL;DR

• Google Home is getting some new features and fixes for speakers, cameras, lights, and thermostats.

• Home Premium users will no longer have to configure all their cameras separately.

• Google’s smoothing out issues with transferring music playback to a new speaker or display.

Big changes are on the way for your Google-powered smart home, with Assistant finally scheduled to go away for good next summer — that’s still months off, though, and in the meantime we’ve got a fresh batch of Google Home updates to check out.

Today Google’s sharing its latest set of new features and bugfixes coming to Home, and it looks like there are quite a few in here that are worth paying attention to. For starters, owners of those affordable Walmart Onn smart cameras can now use Familiar Faces with outdoor models. Other camera upgrades include support for clip feedback when multiple users are configured as admins, as well as manual controls for camera security sirens. We’re also getting bugfixes for event notification previews, event-based video history, and camera controls in landscape view.

Home Premium subscribers can look for a new onboarding flow when adding multiple cameras to their homes, letting you configure premium features all at once.

Setting up a Nest Thermostat? Google’s adding a new feature that lets you clone daily temperature settings, so you can quickly apply the same options across multiple days.

We’ve got a few fixes and improvements related to speakers incoming. Google Home Speaker setup should now proceed with fewer visual glitches, and Google’s resolved an issue with configuring these as stereo pairs. There’s also a handful of fixes for audio issues with Google TV, and you should notice more consistent behavior now when attempting to transfer music between different devices.

If you’ve ever run into problems choosing the perfect color for your RGB smart lights in Google Home on iOS, check out the updated color wheel now rolling out.

In addition to all these improvements to the Home app and smart device operation, Google also shared its latest Gemini for Home enhancements today.

items.title: WhatsApp preps travel eSIM discovery, installation, and management tools
items.summary: WhatsApp could soon be your one-stop shop for all things eSIM.
items.body:
Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

Mobile

WhatsApp preps travel eSIM discovery, installation, and management tools

WhatsApp could soon be your one-stop shop for all things eSIM.

•

Nov 25, 2026 — 4:37 PM ET

•

•

Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• WhatsApp appears to be developing a system for eSIM discovery, purchase, installation, and management.

• Users would be able to search for eSIMs based on specific travel destinations.

• Automated tools could wait to activate the eSIM until you arrive where you’re headed.

WhatsApp just got a big upgrade with the announcement of support for scheduling messages, and now we’re already getting an early look at what could be coming next, as we uncover evidence for what looks like a new travel eSIM feature.

APK teardown

This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

You're reading an Android Authority exclusive story you won’t find anywhere else. An APK teardown helps predict features that may arrive on a service in the future based on work-in-progress code. However, it is possible that such predicted features may not make it to a public release. More Authority Insights →

Looking across the changes present in WhatsApp’s version 2.26.47.10 update, we’re finding multiple references to “Travel eSIM” support. This isn’t yet live in the app, but here’s a preview for how one of the associated screens could be taking shape:

AssembleDebug / Android Authority

Internally, we’re seeing a whole lot of text strings that appear connected to this feature. Here are just a few:

Code

+Travel eSIM installed
+Keep WhatsApp open until it’s done.
+Installing travel eSIM…
+Getting your travel eSIM ready…
+Install it once and use with all your plans.
+Your travel eSIM is ready
+WhatsApp will add a travel eSIM to your phone. Your plan starts when your phone connects in %1$s.
+Install eSIM?
+This phone can’t take this eSIM. It may be locked to a carrier or out of eSIM space.
+Couldn’t install travel eSIM
+This eSIM’s activation code is invalid or has already been used.
+Couldn’t set up your travel eSIM
+Travel eSIMs aren’t available to you yet
+Your plan starts when you turn on your eSIM.
+Couldn’t load plans
+Loading data plans
+Plans aren’t available for this destination
+Your phone didn’t let WhatsApp install this eSIM.
+Installing an eSIM needs a phone with an eSIM chip and a recent version of Android.
+This phone can’t install eSIMs
+Install it now and turn it on when you arrive in %1$s.
+Your plan starts when your phone connects there. You’ll get a message when it does.

Based on what we’ve found so far, we can make a few guesses about how this is likely to operate. It seems that we’ll be able to enter a destination into the app, and WhatsApp would search for compatible eSIM options. Those may not be available for everyone, all at once, as we find “coming soon” messages prepared for both global and regional plans. Options may include fixed-data, as well as unlimited plans.

You can expect to see a few introductory screens helping to educate users about eSIMs, and it sure looks like the app is preparing to integrate with Android’s eSIM installation process.

One handy feature could be an automated system for turning on the eSIM only when we actually reach the destination we intended to use it — freeing us from accidentally plowing through our eSIM data before we really needed it.

Management tools should let you view the eSIMs you’ve purchased so far, seeing which are still available, which are expired, and which have data remaining on them. And along the way, it looks like the app will be able to give you low-data warnings or let you know when a plan is about to end.

Readers' poll

Would you use WhatsApp to buy and install eSIMs?

0 votes

Of course, there’s the possibility your phone may not support this functionality, especially if it’s running an older version of Android. For the moment, at least, we don’t yet have a clear sense for where that cutoff may lie, but expect there to be one.

Finally, WhatsApp might not be preparing this new support on its own, and a “Powered by %1$s” string could suggest that some of this eSIM system may arrive courtesy of a third-party service — we just don’t yet know whose name is going to show up in place of that variable.

All of this sounds pretty nice to our ears. Buying an eSIM is a great option for international travel, and WhatsApp is a great messaging service for travel abroad, so this feels like a match made in heaven. It also looks like WhatsApp is serious about its approach here, and the strings we’ve found paint the picture of quite robust integration. For now, we’ll keep looking for the rest of the details on how this new service offering could be coming together.

items.title: 1Password Security Breach: What Was Accessed and What Wasn't
items.summary: Popular password management app 1Password today said it experienced a security breach earlier this month. 1Password says some customer names and email addresses were accessed, but no customer vault contents were compromised. On November 19, 1Password saw indications that an employee's GitHub account…
items.body: Popular password management app 1Password today said it experienced a security breach earlier this month. 1Password says some customer names and email addresses were accessed, but no customer vault contents were compromised. On November 19, 1Password saw indications that an employee's GitHub account had been breached and began investigating. The company says the breached GitHub account was used to access source code and push malicious code to backend services, with the code downloading some customer data. Here's a list of what the hacker was able to get: Names and email addresses customers use to sign into 1Password Account and user identifiers, and account creation and last sign-in times Public keys Secure Remote Password protocol parameters (1Password says this can't be used for account access) Tokens in emailed links for invitations, provisioning, and account recovery Other non-secret account data related to 1Password's internal architecture, like version numeric identifiers and file numeric identifiers 1Password source code, which 1Password says does not include customer data or user secrets Access to 1Password's CI/CD system, which it says has infrastructure-related secrets for the service to work According to 1Password, there is no impact to its services, availability, or product security. Customer vaults and the items in them were not accessed, nor were the keys that protect vaults. The hacker did not have access to account recovery keys or 1Password apps and browser extensions. 1Password vaults are encrypted and protected by keys on the user end, so content is not accessible to 1Password or anyone who hacks the 1Password servers. The biggest risk comes from the token breach. Tokens can be used for account recovery, but they only work when paired with an SSO sign-in or a six-digit code sent to a user's email address. items.summary: Popular messaging app WhatsApp was today updated with an option to schedule messages, which the company says was one of its most requested features. WhatsApp users can create a message and schedule it to arrive from 10 minutes to 14 days later in one-to-one chats and group chats. Scheduling a messag…
items.body: Popular messaging app WhatsApp was today updated with an option to schedule messages, which the company says was one of its most requested features. WhatsApp users can create a message and schedule it to arrive from 10 minutes to 14 days later in one-to-one chats and group chats. Scheduling a message can be done by pressing and holding the send button after composing and then choosing a date and time. Scheduled messages work with text, photos, and videos, and will still send even if a user's device is offline. There is an option to see all scheduled messages and delete them before they're sent if needed. Scheduled messages are end-to-end encrypted and look like any other WhatsApp message, with no indication on the receiver's end that the message was scheduled. Apple's iMessage service already has a Send Later feature that supports scheduling messages, so WhatsApp is catching up with Apple's built-in messaging option. WhatsApp says scheduled messages are rolling out globally over the coming weeks. TL;DR

• The enough phone is trying to offer a throwback Android experience with its 5.3-inch display and compact, pocket-friendly build.

• When first announced earlier this month, the phone was set to get 8GB of RAM, 128GB storage, and a 3,500mAh battery.

• Instead of that, it will now ship with 12GB of RAM, 256GB storage, and a 3,850mAh silicon-carbon battery.

In 2026, we’ve all started getting used to the idea of phones trying to do more with less, as RAM and chip shortages impact production everywhere, but one upstart is now bucking that trend, as the tiny enough phone scores a surprise spec upgrade.

We first heard of the enough phone earlier this month. The crowdfunded handset was envisioned as a response to design trends that have pushed smartphones into larger and larger territory, prompting its creators to instead go with a 5.3-inch screen that’s much smaller than what you’ll find on the vast majority of handsets out there.

Priced at $449 over on Kickstarter at its current early bird level (the $399 level is already sold out), the handset was initially announced as running a Dimensity 7500 SoC, paired with 8GB of RAM, 128GB internal storage, and getting its power from a 3,500mAh battery — nothing really spectacular there, but what felt like some decent compromises to keep costs down.

With eight days left to go on its crowdfunding effort, enough is now sharing some big upgrades to those specs — and without any change to pricing. Instead of 8GB, the phone will now be equipped with 12GB of RAM. Storage is also getting a boost, climbing from 128GB to 256GB — and that’s even expandable, an all-too-rare feature these days.

Finally, enough is giving the phone a beefier battery. Rather than 3,500mAh, the phone will ship with a 3,850mAh battery. While a 10% boost may not sound like much, enough is also committing to giving the phone a silicon-carbon battery. That should help save space internally, as well as support speedier charging.

Right now, the enough phone is about 85% of the way towards reaching its crowdfunding goal, and the company says it needs roughly 100 more backers to sign on to reach its target. Once that’s over, the final retail price will rise to $599. If anyone out there was on the fence, do these upgrades finally push you over? Let us know down in the comments.

Mobile

WhatsApp catches up to Google Messages with scheduling for texts, photos, and videos

Messages can be set 10 minutes to 14 days ahead of time.

•

Nov 25, 2026 — 1:56 PM ET

•

•

Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• WhatsApp now lets you schedule messages 10 minutes to 14 days ahead of time in individual and group chats.

• The feature works with texts, photos, and video in both one-on-one and group chats.

• Competitors Google Messages, Signal, and Telegram have had scheduled messages for a while.

Lots of things can keep you from being a reliable texter, including thinking of the right thing to say but at the wrong time, and WhatsApp is now able to help out with that by adding support for scheduled messages.

Today, the messaging app announced that it’s adding the ability for users to schedule messages to send at a future point. WhatsApp says this has been one of the features that users requested most. Scheduled messaging was already available on Google Messages, Signal, and Telegram, so it finally brings WhatsApp up to speed with the competition.

WhatsApp

WhatsApp users can set a message to send from 10 minutes to 14 days ahead of time. The feature works with texts, photos, and video in both one-on-one and group chats, and the messages are end-to-end encrypted. The recipient won’t receive any indication that a message has been scheduled.

Scheduled messages are handy for more than making sure not to miss sending birthday greetings on the right day or to avoid waking someone up for just a meme when they’re in another time zone. Because messages are sent even if a user’s phone is off or out of battery at the scheduled time, the feature is also useful for when you know you’ll be unreachable, like when traveling.

WhatsApp said that scheduled messages are rolling out globally starting today. The timing should make it much easier to manage the upcoming holiday season, when sending out greetings can quickly go from heartwarming to overwhelming.

Once you have access to scheduled messages, you can draft a message as usual and then press and hold the send button and pick the date and time you want it to arrive. WhatsApp notes that you can see all of your scheduled messages in your account, and you can delete them before they’re set to send if you change your mind.

items.body: Hong Kong startup Savage Technology has announced its first product, "Orrorin Glasses," promising Vision Pro-style pinch controls and full-color displays for both eyes in a frame weighing just 45 grams. The company describes the glasses as offering "Vision Pro–level interaction" and being around 25 times lighter than Apple's headset, including its external battery. Savage highlights the bulky hardware currently required for Apple's spatial computing experience, although Orrorin offers substantially fewer capabilities. Savage says small pinches performed at the user's side control the interface without a ring, wristband, or controller. Eye tracking makes the display fade when the wearer looks away, rather than selecting interface elements as it does on Vision Pro. That also distinguishes Orrorin from the Meta Ray-Ban Display, which costs the same $799 but has a screen for only the right eye and requires a Neural Band wristband for gesture control. Standard Ray-Ban Meta glasses have no displays. Orrorin lacks positional tracking and spatial mapping , so it cannot anchor virtual windows in a room like Vision Pro. Orrorin is the first product from Savage Technology, co-founded by Bill Pei and Elena Shi, and remains in engineering validation for now. The company is currently targeting developers with third-party apps and interaction with AI agents such as Claude Code and Codex. Apple is expected to launch its first smart glasses next year , although the initial model reportedly will not have displays, instead offering speakers, microphones, and Siri integration. Orrorin reservations start at $29 toward the $799 price. Savage estimates shipments will begin in March 2027 for Founder Edition buyers and May 2027 for Early Bird buyers. items.body: Apple has rules in place that are supposed to protect iPhone users from unwanted advertising in push notifications and Live Activities, but some apps appear to be flouting these rules, and Apple does not appear to be consistently enforcing them. Apple's App Store guidelines do allow iPhone apps to send push notifications for promotions or direct marketing purposes, but only if users have "explicitly opted in to receive them via consent language displayed" in the app, and so long as the app provides a method "for a user to opt out from receiving such messages." The guideline, in part: Push Notifications should not be used for promotions or direct marketing purposes unless customers have explicitly opted in to receive them via consent language displayed in your app's UI, and you provide a method in your app for a user to opt out from receiving such messages. Nothing recently shared more details on the Ear note, a pair of earbuds with a charging case that doubles as an AI audio recorder. The company has now shared a video detailing its new hardware ahead of the December 8 launch.

In a video posted to YouTube and social media platforms, Nothing offers a good look at the Ear note’s design from multiple angles, highlighting the charging case’s hardware buttons, a USB-C port, and more.

While the video offers a decent look at the earbuds and the charging case/AI recorder, the description walks through some features and calls it Nothing’s “best in-ear audio ever.”

Pricing information is currently unavailable, and that’s unlikely to change until the company announces the Ear note on December 8.

Nothing released the Ear 3a earlier this year with audio and call recording support. However, the Ear note takes it a step further with its charging case that serves as a standalone audio recorder.

items.body:

Mobile

Samsung quietly expands Modes and Routines with AI and 7 presets in One UI 9.5

You can ask Gemini or Perplexity, but only Perplexity answers automatically.

•

Nov 25, 2026 — 10:06 AM ET

•

•

Adamya Sharma / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• One UI 9.5 Beta 1 adds an “Ask AI assistant” action to Samsung’s Modes and Routines app that can send prompts to Gemini or Perplexity.

• In our testing, Perplexity automatically sends prompts and reads answers aloud hands-free, whereas Gemini only prefills the prompt and waits for a manual tap because the Google app blocks Samsung’s auto-send request.

• The update also unlocks text summarization, offline translation, image text extraction, and a Repeat loop action. There are also seven new preset routines, including a Morning news briefing that only works hands-free when switched to Perplexity.

Samsung’s Modes and Routines has quietly become one of the most useful parts of One UI for power users. It lets you automate almost anything on your Galaxy phone with simple “if this, then that” rules. With the One UI 9.5 beta, Routines can now hand tasks to an AI assistant as well. Samsung didn’t mention this in the One UI 9.5 beta changelog, but we tried it on our Galaxy S26 Ultra, and which AI assistant you pick makes a big difference.

APK teardown

This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

You're reading an Android Authority exclusive story you won’t find anywhere else. An APK teardown helps predict features that may arrive on a service in the future based on work-in-progress code. However, it is possible that such predicted features may not make it to a public release. More Authority Insights →

Routines can now ask Gemini or Perplexity for you

Modes and Routines v5.2.00.69 in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 adds a new action called “Ask AI assistant.” You pick an assistant, type a prompt into the “Enter command” box, and the routine sends it whenever its trigger fires, whether that’s dismissing your alarm, arriving at work, or tapping a button. The prompt can also include text from earlier actions in the routine, going up to 8,000 characters.

Gemini and Perplexity are the only two options for Ask AI assistant, and they appear only if their apps are installed. Both are built into the Routines app, so you can’t add other AI assistants like ChatGPT or Claude. Routines still has a separate “Ask Bixby” action from One UI 9, too.

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

There’s a catch, though: Routines can only launch the assistant. It doesn’t wait for an answer or receive one from the assistant, so you can’t feed the AI’s response back into a later action like a pop-up or a note. The routine finishes as soon as the assistant opens.

Perplexity answers on its own, but Gemini waits for you

With Perplexity, Routines opens the app’s floating assistant with the prompt and tells it to send the prompt right away:

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

In our testing, once the routine was triggered, Perplexity searched the web, answered in its overlay with sources, and read the answer aloud, without us touching the phone.

Gemini is a different story, though. Routines first tries to send the prompt automatically through a Google app service. If that fails, it falls back to sharing the text with the Gemini app, which only prefills the prompt.

On our Galaxy S26 Ultra, the Google app (v17.76.14) rejected Samsung’s request, so Routines used the fallback. Gemini opened full screen with our prompt typed in, and then waited for us to tap Send (which kind of defeats the convenience of a routine).

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

Seemingly, the Google app only lets Google’s own apps use this service (for now), so Samsung’s automation has to stop halfway. Google could add Samsung Routines to that allowlist before One UI 9.5’s stable release. Until then, Perplexity is the only assistant that works hands-free in a routine. This is a nice win for Samsung’s growing partnership with Perplexity, even though the limitation likely comes from Google’s side.

The new Morning news briefing preset doesn’t work as advertised with Gemini

This disparity in auto-send behavior in Perplexity vs Gemini matters most for one of the seven new preset routines. “Morning news briefing” runs when you dismiss your alarm, and Samsung describes it like this:

Code

<string name="preset_name_morning_news">Morning news briefing</string>
<string name="preset_description_morning_news">When you dismiss your alarm, a summary of the latest news in society, business, and the stock market is read aloud.</string>
<string name="preset_param_morning_news">Summarize today's top news in 2-3 highlights for society, business, and the stock market.</string>

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

Save 42% on Dreame's self-emptying, mop-washing robot with 25,000Pa suction ahead of Black Friday.

Dreame’s D30 Ultra CE handles vacuuming and mopping, then looks after itself at the base station, which makes it one of the more hands-off robots at this price. The Dreame D30 Ultra CE is now $349.99 on Amazon, down from $599.99. That’s $250 (42%) off and a new all-time low.

Suction is rated at 25,000Pa, and dual detangling brushes help keep hair from wrapping around the roller. For mopping, two rotating pads scrub the floor, and Dreame’s MopExtend RoboSwing tech swings a pad out toward baseboards and corners as the robot reaches a wall.

Ultrasonic carpet detection tells the robot when it’s on a rug, so it can lift its mops by up to 10.5mm and keep them dry. LiDAR navigation maps your home, and Dreame’s 3DAdapt system helps it steer around obstacles.

Back at the all-in-one base station, the robot empties its dust bin into a bag that holds up to 100 days of debris, and the station washes and dries the mop pads for you. That leaves you with little more than topping up the clean water tank and emptying the dirty one now and then.

You can set room-specific cleaning schedules in the Dreame app, and the D30 Ultra CE also works with Alexa and Google Home for voice control.

Big over-ear headphones can eat up a lot of space in a carry-on, which is where the Soundcore Space One Pro come in. They fold down to about half their size, and they’re now $113.99 on Amazon, $86 (43%) off their $199.99 list price and matching their lowest price.

Soundcore’s FlexiCurve design is what lets the headphones shrink so much, so they slip into a backpack or tote far more easily than most noise canceling cans. Once you’re on the plane, train, or bus, adaptive noise canceling adjusts in real time to cut out engine rumble and chatter. The pressure-relieving headband is designed with long-haul comfort in mind.

Battery life is rated at up to 40 hours with ANC on and up to 60 hours with it off, enough for several long-haul flights. A five-minute charge adds around eight hours of playback, and a 3.5mm cable lets you plug into in-flight entertainment.

LDAC support means higher-quality streaming from compatible Android phones, and multipoint lets you stay connected to two devices at once. Four mics with an AI algorithm handle calls, and Hear ID 2.0 can tailor the sound to your hearing. Amazon shoppers rate the Soundcore Space One Pro 4.4 stars from more than 2,900 reviews.
